title: Warehouse vs Data Lake vs Lakehouse
interviewAnswer: Warehouses emphasize managed structured analytics; data lakes store flexible files/objects; lakehouse approaches add table metadata, transactions and governance over object storage. The right choice depends on workload and organizational needs.
why: Warehouse vs Data Lake vs Lakehouse is a recurring foundation across data science and machine learning because it affects both theoretical correctness and practical system behavior.
deepDive: Warehouses emphasize managed structured analytics; data lakes store flexible files/objects; lakehouse approaches add table metadata, transactions and governance over object storage. The right choice depends on workload and organizational needs. Table formats add schema/evolution/transaction semantics. Compute-storage separation changes scaling/cost. The interview-level skill is not merely recalling the definition: explain the assumptions, what diagnostic evidence you would inspect, and what alternative you would choose when those assumptions fail.
workedExample: Raw logs land in object storage while curated analytical tables expose reliable schemas for BI and ML.
commonMistakes: Using the concept mechanically without checking assumptions or data semantics.
Reporting one metric/result without examining uncertainty, slices or failure modes.
followUps: What assumptions or limitations does Warehouse vs Data Lake vs Lakehouse have?
How would you validate Warehouse vs Data Lake vs Lakehouse on a real dataset?
production: In production, make assumptions explicit, validate on representative slices, compare with a simple baseline and monitor the signals that can drift.
